concerns.text: FR-004 mandates enumerating 'all n-node subgraphs' but the Assumptions section explicitly scopes the investigation to '3-node motifs only'. This creates a direct contradiction between a general requirement and a scoped assumption. FR-004 must be revised to specify 'all 3-node subgraphs' to align with the project scope.

FR-005 requires partial correlations 'controlling for global node degree' but does not specify whether this refers to the structural graph (predictor) or the functional graph (outcome). The Edge Cases and Assumptions sections do not clarify this. Without this definition, the requirement is ambiguous and risks circular logic (as noted in the kickback concerns regarding tautology).

FR-004 requires generating 'degree-preserved null networks' but the Assumptions section does not explicitly commit to a graph directionality (directed vs. undirected). The Maslov-Sneppen rewiring algorithm and motif definitions differ significantly between these regimes. The spec must explicitly state the graph type (e.,g., 'undirected binary adjacency') to ensure the null model is valid.

FR-005 mandates 'Bonferroni correction' but does not address the potential multicollinearity between motif z-scores (predictors). The kickback concerns highlight that running 13 separate partial correlations without handling inter-correlation inflates Type I error. The requirement should either mandate a multivariate regression approach or explicitly require a VIF threshold check before univariate testing.
SC-003 contains a typo: 'tested ‑node motifs' (missing the number '3'). This should be corrected to 'tested 3-node motifs' to maintain consistency with the scope defined in Assumptions and FR-004.

The Assumptions section cites 'Schaefer et al.,' with a missing year and DOI. While this is a citation issue, it creates ambiguity in the 'Verified Accuracy' principle (Constitution Principle II) regarding the validity of the parcellation assumption.
